metadata.summary: Nicolas Jackson scored his eighth goal in 10 games but an error from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki meant Aston Villa had to settle for a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham.
metadata.content: Aston Villa 1 - 1 Fulham - Match Report & Highlights Skip to main content Aston Villa vs Fulham; Premier League FT Full Time AET After Extra Time LIVE This is a live match. Aston Villa 1 N Jackson ( 39' 39th minute ) Fulham 1 Z Suzuki ( 64' 64th minute og own goal ) Watch match highlights Close Latest Premier League Odds Get Sky Sports Get a NOW Sports Membership Watch Live Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham: Zion Suzuki concedes own goal as Nicholas Jackson scores after John McGinn's penalty miss in draw with Fulham Report and free match highlights as Aston Villa are held to a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham Saturday 31 October 2026 22:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Fulham. Nicolas Jackson scored his eighth goal in 10 games but an error from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki meant Aston Villa had to settle for a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham. Villa should have gone ahead after 15 minutes when they were awarded a penalty following a review when Sander Berge was penalised for a handball in the box as he jumped with Leon Goretzka at a corner. With neither Emi Buendia nor Ross Barkley in the line-up, John McGinn stepped up to take the penalty but the Scotland international - who had only ever taken a penalty for Villa in a shoot-out - smashed the ball against the crossbar and over.

messages.text: Hamilton claims first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City GP

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell in qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP Qualifying: Lewis Hamilton claims first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP Qualifying: Lewis Hamilton claims first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell Lewis Hamilton claims first grand prix pole position for Ferrari in Mexico City; Hamilton edged out George Russell for first pole since July 2023; watch Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm) to see if Kimi Antonelli can become champion, live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 31 October 2026 23:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell in qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix. Hamilton had been outpaced by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc throughout the weekend but the 41-year-old produced his best lap when it mattered most at the end of Q3 to edge out Russell by nine thousandths of a second. The seven-time world champion has twice claimed Sprint poles since his move from Mercedes to Ferrari at the start of the 2025 season but will now start a grand prix from the front of the grid for the first time since July 2023 after extending his record tally to 105 poles. metadata.summary: Alex Mitchell provided an injury worry for England ahead of the Nations Championship as the scrum-half was forced off during Northampton's 28-14 win against Gloucester on Saturday evening.
metadata.content: Prem Rugby: England's Alex Mitchell injured as Northampton Saints, Bath, Saracens, Harlequins pick up victories | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Prem Rugby: England's Alex Mitchell injured as Northampton Saints, Bath, Saracens, Harlequins pick up victories Saturday's Prem Rugby sees Northampton Saints beat Gloucester, Bath defeat Sale Sharks, Harlequins win at Exeter Chiefs and Saracens beat Newcastle Red Bulls; Northampton scrum-half Alex Mitchell an England worry as he suffers early injury at Franklin's Gardens Saturday 31 October 2026 20:19, UK Image: Northampton Saints scrum-half Alex Mitchell is an England injury worry ahead of the Nations Championship after departing early on Saturday Alex Mitchell provided an injury worry for England ahead of the Nations Championship as the scrum-half was forced off during Northampton's 28-14 win against Gloucester on Saturday evening. Mitchell had to come off with just 21 minutes played due to a hamstring injury, walking down the Franklin's Gardens tunnel to be replaced by 20-year-old Jonny Weimann. That will be a concern for England boss Steve Borthwick ahead of the game against Australia at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham next weekend, but Northampton did not let their loss stop them from defeating in-form Gloucester. messages.text: Alcaraz reaches first Vienna final as De Minaur upsets Zverev

metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz reached the Vienna Open final for the first time after beating Daniil Medvedev 6-4 7-6 (7-2) on Saturday. He will face Alex de Minaur, who upset Alexander Zverev in the final.
metadata.content: Vienna Open: Carlos Alcaraz beats Daniil Medvedev to reach first final as Alex de Minaur stuns Alexander Zverev | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Vienna Open: Carlos Alcaraz beats Daniil Medvedev to reach first final as Alex de Minaur stuns Alexander Zverev Carlos Alcaraz beats Daniil Medvedev as Alex de Minaur stuns Alexander Zverev to set up Vienna Open final; Watch Alcaraz vs De Minaur in Vienna Open final live on Sky Sports Tennis on Sunday at 1pm ; watch ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Nov 2 Saturday 31 October 2026 20:10, UK Image: Carlos Alcaraz is through to the Vienna Open final for the first time, and will face Alex de Minaur on Sunday for the title Carlos Alcaraz reached the Vienna Open final for the first time after beating Daniil Medvedev 6-4 7-6 (7-2) on Saturday. He will face Alex de Minaur, who upset Alexander Zverev in the final. Alcaraz reached the 37th tour-level final of his career and his fifth of the year, while extending his winning streak at ATP 500 events to 25 matches. The second seed took the opening set after Medvedev double-faulted to hand him set point. The Russian responded strongly in the second, however, forcing a tie-break. With neither player able to establish a decisive advantage, Alcaraz unleashed a barrage of powerful groundstrokes in the breaker to seal victory in 96 minutes. metadata.content: Oliver Glasner: Nottingham Forest head coach reveals anger, desire to change growing pattern at club amid poor start to season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Oliver Glasner: Nottingham Forest head coach reveals anger, desire to change growing pattern at club amid poor start to season Nottingham Forest were beaten 2-0 by Brentford and remain in the relegation zone; Oliver Glasner's side are the lowest scorers in the Premier League this season and it has prompted an angry response from the Forest head coach; Glasner is Forest's fifth head coach since August 2025 Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Saturday 31 October 2026 19:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner reacted to his team's loss to Brentford in the Premier League. There is no more Mr Nice Guy at Nottingham Forest, according to Oliver Glasner. The Austrian has said he will change things at the club and if the players don't buy into it, they will be looking for their sixth manager in just over a year. Forest fans booed off their team after a 2-0 loss at Brentford left them in the relegation zone for another week. They are also the Premier League's lowest scorers this season with six goals from nine games. messages.text: Norris pips Antonelli in final practice to set up thrilling Mexico qualifying

metadata.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris pipped Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.001s in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix to set up a thrilling qualifying.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP: Lando Norris pips Kimi Antonelli in final practice to set up thrilling Mexico qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP: Lando Norris pips Kimi Antonelli in final practice to set up thrilling Mexico qualifying Lando Norris and Kimi Antonelli were separated by just 0.001s at the top of the timesheet in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix; watch qualifying later at 9pm with Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Saturday 31 October 2026 19:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's David Croft and Karun Chandok discuss Esteban Ocon being replaced by Haas for the Mexico City GP, Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen being handed a grid penalty for their P2 collision and Isack Hajar's paddock altercation with a fan McLaren's Lando Norris pipped Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.001s in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix to set up a thrilling qualifying. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc had topped both of Friday's practice sessions but McLaren and Mercedes showed their hand to outpace the Monegasque driver by one tenth of a second. Antonelli is likely to become world champion in Sunday's race as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure the Formula 1 drivers' title.
